title: Neighborhood trust is practically resilient but socially under-connected, especially for young adults
source_unit: Nextdoor/The Harris Poll, Most Americans Still Rely on Their Neighbors, September 28, 2026

observations.period: April 16-20, 2026 survey fieldwork, published September 28, 2026; practical neighborhood reliance

trust_strengthened.unit: percent saying trust in their neighborhood strengthened over the past five years

trust_weakened.unit: percent saying neighborhood trust weakened over the past five years

neighbor_help.unit: percent saying they could call on a neighbor for help if needed

neighborhood_belonging.unit: percent feeling a sense of belonging where they live

mutual_aid_route.value: Neighborhood social infrastructure can remain operational even when broad narratives describe social trust as uniformly declining.

observations.method: Online Harris Poll conducted for Nextdoor in the United States; results weighted for demographic and political characteristics where necessary to align with population proportions.
observations.uncertainty: This is a commissioned, cross-sectional online survey using respondents who agreed to participate; reported trust and willingness to seek help are not observed assistance, repeated contact, or a causal neighborhood effect.
observations.subgroup: U.S. adults age 18+; the publication reports age, region, and other subgroup comparisons.
observations.counterinterpretation: People may report generalized reliance or belonging without using it during a real shock; the apparent improvement may reflect recall, question framing, or selective participation.

observations.period: April 16-20, 2026 survey fieldwork, published September 28, 2026; desired versus experienced connection

want_more_interaction.unit: percent wanting more interaction with neighbors than they currently have

young_adult_loneliness.unit: percent of adults ages 18-24 feeling lonely or socially isolated at least sometimes

overall_loneliness.unit: percent of adults overall feeling lonely or socially isolated at least sometimes

young_adult_welcomed.unit: percent of adults ages 18-24 feeling welcomed or included by neighbors, versus 41% overall

connection_option_gap.value: The strongest neighborhood connection gap is not necessarily refusal of community; it is a lack of low-stakes routes into belonging for younger adults.

observations.method: Cross-sectional online survey with subgroup estimates reported by age.
observations.uncertainty: The subgroup base and exact question wording are not fully reproduced in the publication summary; loneliness, welcome, and desired interaction are self-reports and not measures of social-network size or service access.
observations.subgroup: Adults ages 18-24 compared with U.S. adults overall.
observations.counterinterpretation: Young adults may be more willing to name loneliness or desire for interaction than older adults, so differences may partly reflect reporting norms.

observations.period: April 16-20, 2026 survey fieldwork, published September 28, 2026; local recommendation trust

neighbor_recommendation_trust.unit: percent trusting neighbors a lot or completely for contractor or local-service recommendations

online_review_trust.unit: percent trusting online reviews a lot or completely for contractor or local-service recommendations

influencer_recommendation_trust.unit: percent trusting social-media influencers a lot or completely for contractor or local-service recommendations

proximity_accountability.value: Local recommendation trust may derive from proximity and repeat accountability rather than from abstract platform reputation alone.

observations.method: Cross-sectional online survey; respondents rated information sources for local contractor and service recommendations.
observations.uncertainty: Trust ratings are not verified recommendation accuracy, completed purchases, service quality, or remedy; the platform sponsor may make neighborhood-mediated routes more salient.
observations.counterinterpretation: Neighbors may be trusted because recommendations are socially visible, not necessarily because they provide better information than reviews or influencers.

observations.period: April 16-20, 2026 survey fieldwork, published September 28, 2026; trust-building infrastructure

day_to_day_interaction.unit: percent naming regular day-to-day interactions as what strengthens neighbor trust

long_term_residency.unit: percent naming long-term residency as a trust-strengthening condition

neighborhood_apps.unit: percent naming neighborhood apps or online groups

communication_barrier.unit: percent naming lack of communication as what most weakens neighbor trust

infrastructure_mechanism.value: Digital tools may lower the cost of repeated contact, but the reported trust-building mechanism is recurring interaction rather than app use by itself.

observations.method: Cross-sectional online survey with multiple-response trust-builder and trust-barrier items.
observations.uncertainty: The estimates identify perceived mechanisms, not experimental effects of apps, events, public space, or residency; categories may overlap and the sponsor is a neighborhood platform.
observations.counterinterpretation: People who already trust neighbors may be more likely to value or participate in repeated interaction, so the direction of influence is unresolved.

related_sources.claim: Official Nextdoor publication page containing survey results, subgroup contrasts, recommendation-trust findings, and methodology.
Adjacent American Neighbor Survey evidence provides a separate class and neighborhood-socializing comparison; it is not treated as the same survey or merged estimate.

boundary: This record adds a neighborhood social-infrastructure route: practical mutual aid and local recommendation trust can persist alongside an unmet desire for connection, with a sharper welcome gap among young adults. It does not establish actual assistance, completed local-service outcomes, causal app effects, or durable community recovery. The source is platform-commissioned, cross-sectional, and based on an online opt-in panel.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Nextdoor publication page was reviewed for publication date, survey sample, weighting, practical reliance, young-adult connection gap, recommendation trust, trust-building mechanisms, and methodological limits.
